lean.statement:
{f : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f)
    (hlo : ∀ z v, α * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v) v)
    (hup : ∀ z v, (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v) v ≤ β * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (x y : E) :
    let φ := fun t : ℝ => continuousLinearMapOfBilin
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)))
    let H := ∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, φ t
    IntervalIntegrable φ volume 0 1 ∧
      gradient f x - gradient f y = H (x - y) ∧
      H.IsSymmetric ∧
      (∀ v, α * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (H v) v ∧
        inner ℝ (H v) v ≤ β * ‖v‖ ^ 2) ∧
      ‖H‖ ≤ max |α| |β|
approved_definition_context: E is any complete real inner-product space; its norm is induced by that inner product. f is a real-valued map, ContDiff R 2 f is global twice continuously Frechet differentiable. fderiv R (fderiv R f) z is the genuine nested second Frechet derivative, evaluated successively on two vectors.

continuousLinearMapOfBilin sends an actual continuous real bilinear form B to its Riesz operator A, characterized by inner(A v,w)=B(v,w). It is a definition of the operator, not a certificate premise. gradient f is the Riesz representative of the Frechet derivative of f.

The notation integral t in0..1 denotes ordinary Lebesgue Bochner interval integration, here with values in the complete normed space of continuous real linear operators E->E. IntervalIntegrable phi volume0 1 means actual integrability on that interval.

H.IsSymmetric means for every v,w, inner(Hv,w)=inner(v,Hw). The norm of H is its induced operator norm. alpha,beta are arbitrary real scalars. There is no supplied matrix, operator identity, symmetry or integrability premise, and no probability law.
